subject: Error in  INLA  with SPDE  in Bayesian spatial  model

messages.author: eed057bc7db4910e
messages.subject: Error in  INLA  with SPDE  in Bayesian spatial  model
parts:
Dear all 
I have tried to fit spatial Bayesian model in sub Saharan Africa  with INLA  with SPDE and the mesh and everything have worked but the last spatial model is not working and how can i fix that 

the code i have been working on 
#####the libraries i have used ######
library(fmesher)
library(INLA)
library(glmnet)
library(here)
###########
library(sf)
library(haven)
library(dplyr)

# Load your dataset
mylast <- read_dta("/finally lets goo2.dta")

# Drop rows with missing coordinates only
mylast_clean <- mylast %>%
  filter(!is.na(LATNUM), !is.na(LONGNUM))

# Convert to sf object
mylast_sf <- st_as_sf(mylast_clean, coords = c("LONGNUM", "LATNUM"), crs = 4326)

######
library(sp)
library(sf)
coo <-cbind(mylast_clean$LONGNUM, mylast$LATNUM)
#project the adminisrative boundary

st_crs(sub_saharan_africa) <- 4326
#convert a spatial polygon object into a format that can be used to define the boundary of a mesh
bdry<-inla.sp2segment(sub_saharan_africa) 

######

bdry$loc <-inla.mesh.map(bdry$loc)

mesh <- inla.mesh.2d(
  loc = coo,                  # Coordinates of your data points
  boundary = bdry,            # The boundary object created from the shapefile
  max.edge = c(0.5, 1),       # Maximum edge length for the mesh triangles
  max.n = c(48000, 16000),    # Maximum number of nodes in the interior and exterior of the mesh
  max.n.strict = c(128000, 128000), # Strict maximum number of nodes
  cutoff = 0.1,               # Minimum distance between points to avoid very small triangles
  offset = c(0.5, 1)          # Extension of the mesh beyond the boundary (buffer zone)
)
plot(mesh)
points(coo,col="blue") 

#######stack producing 

# Load required libraries
library(INLA)
library(sf)

# Create the Projection Matrix
A <- inla.spde.make.A(
  mesh = mesh,
  loc = as.matrix(cbind(mylast_clean$LONGNUM, mylast_clean$LATNUM))
)

# Define the SPDE Model
spde <- inla.spde2.matern(mesh, alpha = 2)

# Define the Index for the Spatial Field
iset <- inla.spde.make.index(name = "spatial.field", n.spde = spde$n.spde)

# Create the INLA Stack with all predictors included
stk <- inla.stack(
  data = list(
    y = mylast_clean$teen_preg_status,
    n = mylast_clean$age
  ),
  A = list(A, 1),
  effects = list(
    # Random and spatial effects
    c(iset, list(Intercept = 1)),

    # Fixed effects
    list(
      cluster = mylast_clean$v0010,
      latitude = mylast_clean$LATNUM,
      longitude = mylast_clean$LONGNUM,
      resedence = factor(mylast_clean$resedence),
      sexofhe = factor(mylast_clean$sexofhe),
      educ_stat = factor(mylast_clean$educ_stat),
      media = factor(mylast_clean$media),
      marital_status = factor(mylast_clean$marital_status),
      wealthindex = factor(mylast_clean$wealthindex) , age = mylast_clean$age

    )
  ),
  tag = 'est'
)

###########the spatial bayesian model i have fitted and the problem i have incountered ############

# Prior on the fixed effects
prior.fixed <- list(mean.intercept = 0,
                    prec.intercept = 1,
                    mean = 0, prec = 1)
# Define the Model Formula with Intercept Removed
formula1 <- y ~  -1 + age +resedence +sexofhe + educ_stat + media + marital_status +
  wealthindex + f(spatial.field, model = spde) + f(cluster, model = "iid")

# Fit the Model with INLA  binomial
model1 <- INLA::inla(
  formula1,
  data = inla.stack.data(stk, spde = spde),
  family = "binomial",
  Ntrials = inla.stack.data(stk)$n,
  control.predictor = list(A = inla.stack.A(stk), compute = TRUE),
  control.compute = list(
    dic = TRUE,
    waic = TRUE,
    config = TRUE,
    cpo = TRUE
  ) , verbose=TRUE
)
